title: What is the major challenge you experience with AI game dev?
author: AgenticGameDev
selftext: I wounder what is the major problem when interacting with the LLM that you are experience? Is it usage, speed or that the LLM is missing things that it shouldn't..... What is the real problem you experience in the day to day interactions with e.g. Claude Code?

comments.author: Time_Series4689
comments.body:
1. Cost of tokens


2. Expertise to convert requirements into prompts


3. LLM inability to get sensorial feedback, ie. UI


4. LLM inabilitty to understand other spaces than token relation, ie. spatial, sensorial, emotional, etc.

replies.author: macuseri686
replies.body:
Using a normal AI model like Nano Banana wont work for assets such as spritesheets and pixel art, because AI models cant output transparency, and image models alone have no understanding of animation.

Most pixel-sprite AIs (like Retro Diffusion) are pretty limited. They’re mainly tuned for bipedal humans and usually only give you idle/walk cycles, which breaks down fast once you need monsters, turrets, creatures, vehicles, or non-humanoid stuff.

That gap is actually why I built GameLab Studio (https://gamelabstudio.co). It’s designed for game assets, not just characters, and it’ll generate consistent pixel-art sprites, animations and full transparent bg spritesheets for anything: creatures, machines, towers, VFX, projectiles, etc. Animations aren’t locked to walk/idle either; you can generate attack, fire, spin, explode, transform, whatever the gameplay needs.

It also enforces consistency across scale, palette, and angles, by using already generated angles of the same asset for reference, so you don’t end up with “AI asset soup” during prototyping.

We also have a seamless tileable edge-aware texture generation model

comments.author: TheFlyingR0cket
comments.body:
I found that Claude code or any coding LLM stuck at the structure of a program, Like it's find if it something small, like a chrome extension ect. But if it's large it like a game, it struggles to get the whole structure and if you want to change something large half way through it struggles to get rid of the existing idea as it was part of core structure at the start. 

Too fix this a built a program that had agents that you put your idea into and it goes through a ton of different agents to plan the idea & structure out, and then in spits off a .md file that is 150-200 lines long with a full structure and tasks on how to built it, then I tell Claude code to me read it and then build it. It's still a working progress, but it seems to be going well. 

  
If anyone has an idea they want me to run through it please post below and I'm send you the .md file and then I can analyse the output and make the program better.

replies.author: TheFlyingR0cket
replies.body:
Here is what it is at the moment 

    # Agents Quick Reference
    
    
    ## Pipeline Order
    
    
    ```
    Idea → CEO → Product → Design → Engineer ←→ Critic
         → Architecture → File Registry
         → [Phase] → Task → Implement ←→ Code Reviewer
         → Project Analyzer → [Repair ×3]
         → Summary → Learning
    ```
    
    
    ---
    
    
    ## Agents
    
    
    | Agent | File | What it does |
    |-------|------|--------------|
    | 
    **CEO**
     | `ceo_agent.py` | Interprets the raw idea. Infers project type, defines vision, scope, out-of-scope constraints, and technical constraints. |
    | 
    **Product**
     | `product_agent.py` | Expands the CEO vision into a product spec: user stories, core features, data model, MVP scope. |
    | 
    **Design**
     | `design_agent.py` | Produces UX/UI spec: page layouts, navigation flow, component hierarchy, design system tokens. |
    | 
    **Engineer**
     | `engineer_agent.py` | Converts product + design into a technical engineering plan: stack, modules, APIs, auth, file structure. |
    | 
    **Critic**
     | `critic_agent.py` | Reviews the engineering plan and issues PASS or FAIL with critique bullets. Loops with Engineer until PASS. |
    | 
    **Architecture**
     | `architecture_agent.py` | Turns the approved engineering plan into a concrete file tree and module-to-file mapping (MODULE FILES). |
    | 
    **File Registry**
     | `file_registry_agent.py` | Normalizes and enriches the architecture file list into a registry with descriptions, roles, and path normalization. |
    | 
    **Phase**
     | `phase_agent.py` | Splits the file registry into ordered build phases with dependency resolution (topological sort). Optional — enabled per config. |
    | 
    **Task**
     | `task_agent.py` | Breaks a phase (or the whole project) into implementation tasks: create_file / modify_file / integrate_module, with depends_on ordering. |
    | 
    **Implement**
     | `implement_agent.py` | Writes or modifies the actual code for a single task. Language-aware (Python vs JS/TS). Returns file contents. |
    | 
    **Code Reviewer**
     | `code_reviewer_agent.py` | Reviews implemented code for each task. Issues PASS or FAIL with feedback. Optional — enabled per config. |
    | 
    **Summary**
     | `summary_agent.py` | After a phase completes, summarizes what was built (exported contracts, key decisions) to pass context into the next phase. |
    | 
    **Project Analyzer**
     | `project_analyzer_agent.py` | Scans the generated project for issues: missing files, empty files, broken imports, unused references. Feeds the repair loop. |
    | 
    **Learning**
     | `learning_agent.py` | After a run, reflects on what went well/wrong and writes reusable learnings to guide future runs. |
    | 
    **Marketing**
     | `marketing_agent.py` | Generates a marketing brief (channels, messaging, positioning) from the vision and product spec. Runs separately from the main pipeline. |
    | 
    **File Tree**
     | `file_tree_agent.py` | Legacy/optional. Generates a visual file tree. Not in the active pipeline — Architecture produces this directly. |
    | 
    **Readme**
     | `readme_agent.py` | Generates a README.md for the project from the plan and file tree. Runs at the end of a successful build. |

replies.author: TheFlyingR0cket
replies.body:
**So this was the input/idea.** 

Build a multiplayer tower defense game.



Players cooperatively place, upgrade, and remove defensive structures 

(towers, walls, traps) on a shared grid to survive enemy waves.



Core requirements:

\- Grid-based build system with placement validation (collision, resources, build rules)

\- Data-driven structure definitions (type, cost, stats, upgrade paths)

\- Enemy wave system with basic pathfinding toward player structures

\- Networking abstraction layer — implementation-agnostic, swappable backend

\- Input abstraction — mouse/keyboard, extensible to AI or remote players

\- Save/load system for mid-session persistence

\- 100+ tests (unit + integration) covering all major systems



Architecture constraints:

\- All systems decoupled via interfaces (networking, input, validation, persistence)

\- Networking layer must wrap any backend (e.g. WebSockets, WebRTC) without 

  leaking implementation details into game logic

\- AI-controlled builders must be supportable via the same input abstraction 

  as human players



Deliver:

\- Full project file structure

\- Module responsibilities and interface boundaries

\- Data flow between systems

  
[Then this is the output ](https://wormhole.app/4xDa1X#8THX4HQUW_vbqCaKmfb6vw)

comments.author: ViolinistTemporary
comments.body:
I'm using codex. Here are the problems with it:  

* It can't do UI at all. Especially modifying an aspect is a nightmare. 
* If you don't review the code it writes, your performance is going to tank sooner or later.
* It can't do balancing at all. If you're making a complex, feature-heavy game, you'll need human supervision.
* It can do what you want in coding %99 time, but 1% of the time, oh boy, you're going to spend so many tokens to just fix some simple bug.
* You need to be very coherent when you describe a new feature.

Other than these, it works great, and this is the worst it will ever be, so it's the way forward. Feel free to DM me if you have any questions.
